pitch_detail.notes: From the far side of Colchuck Lake, hike up and gain the moraine, follow it right to the couloir entrance at the glacier's edge.
Climb steep snow filling the gully.
As snow thins later in the season, a few short Class 4 rock steps are exposed.
Top-out can be guarded by a cornice that has required over an hour to breach in some reported conditions.
Scrambling from the Pyramid notch on solid rock with ample protection.
Low 5th class moves on quality rock to the summit; about 5.3 with selective route-finding; holding strictly to the crest adds two steps near 5.6 and 5.7.
Long forest/subalpine trail; the modern approach adds a closed-road walk/bike before the historic trailhead.
Meadow and talus trail to the last camp before the glacier.
pitch_detail.pitch: Goat Flats to Tin Can Gap

pitch_detail.notes: Ice axe and crampons required; crevasse hazard.
pitch_detail.pitch: Tin Can Gap across the Queest-Alb Glacier edge

pitch_detail.notes: Three fixed ladders (rebar/timber anchored) gain the blasted summit block and L-4 lookout cabin at ~6,850 ft.
